-- ── Difficulty coloring ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The six bands and their exact colors are the reference's contract, not a palette of ours: -- ref-QuestLogFrame.lua's table (l.14-20) and GetDifficultyColor (l.584-599, "Used for -- quests and enemy coloration" — the ref's own comment; the TARGET FRAME's level number -- colors through this same function, TargetFrame_CheckLevel l.130), and `QuestDifficultyColor` -- is a name addons read, so both the global and its six keys are fixed. The green→grey -- boundary is the real GetQuestGreenRange() binding (benilla-ui unit.rs — the byte-verified -- grey band the plate/tooltip share; the binding's own byte read is under the 2026-07-17 -- wow-re §5). This retires the BenillaQuestDifficultyColor INTERIM and its approximated -- -2/-10 thresholds. QuestDifficultyColor = { impossible = { r = 1.00, g = 0.10, b = 0.10 }, verydifficult = { r = 1.00, g = 0.50, b = 0.25 }, difficult = { r = 1.00, g = 1.00, b = 0.00 }, standard = { r = 0.25, g = 0.75, b = 0.25 }, trivial = { r = 0.50, g = 0.50, b = 0.50 }, header = { r = 0.70, g = 0.70, b = 0.70 }, }
-- How far ABOVE the player the quest sits picks the band. Note the shape of the last two -- tests: the three hard bands are fixed offsets, but the green/grey boundary is not a -- constant at all — GetQuestGreenRange() widens as the player levels — which is why it is -- asked rather than compared against a number, and why "trivial" is what is left over -- rather than a band with an edge of its own. function GetDifficultyColor(level) local levelDiff = level - UnitLevel("player") if levelDiff >= 5 then return QuestDifficultyColor.impossible elseif levelDiff >= 3 then return QuestDifficultyColor.verydifficult elseif levelDiff >= -2 then return QuestDifficultyColor.difficult elseif -levelDiff <= GetQuestGreenRange() then return QuestDifficultyColor.standard end return QuestDifficultyColor.trivial end
-- ── The list page ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- `mouseButton` is arg1 off RegisterForClicks("LeftButtonUp", "RightButtonUp") -- (BenillaQuestLogTitleTemplate's OnLoad). The watch toggle is SHIFT+left-click, the ref's -- own fork (QuestLogFrame.lua:469-505) — the modifier plumbing this file's header once -- named as the missing engine slice landed with the cursor arc (0216/0218 follow-up), so -- the documented right-click substitute is retired. function BenillaQuestLogTitle_OnClick(button, mouseButton) local index = button.questIndex if not index then return end local _, _, _, isHeader, isCollapsed = GetQuestLogTitle(index) if isHeader then -- pin §5, QuestLog_SetSelection (QuestLogFrame.lua:321-329): a header never becomes -- the selection, it only (un)collapses. No header ever ships in v1 (module doc, -- `benilla-ui/src/script/quest_log.rs`) so Expand/CollapseQuestHeader don't exist yet -- — guarded rather than assumed absent forever. if isCollapsed and type(ExpandQuestHeader) == "function" then ExpandQuestHeader(index) elseif type(CollapseQuestHeader) == "function" then CollapseQuestHeader(index) end return end -- pin §5, QuestLogTitleButton_OnClick (QuestLogFrame.lua:469-501): shift-click either -- posts the quest's NAME into an open chat edit box (l.478-480) or, with chat closed, -- toggles the watch (l.481-500 — the ref's own `else`). Chat wins; the watch is the -- fallback, not the other way round (decision 1059). -- -- The insert (l.480) is `gsub(this:GetText(), " *(.*)", "%1")` — the row LABEL with its -- leading indent trimmed, i.e. the bare quest name; note it is plain text, NOT a -- hyperlink (1.12 has no |Hquest: link). We read `GetQuestLogTitle(index)` instead of -- the label, because our label is not the ref's: this window appends the Complete/Failed -- tag onto the ONE title string (the v1 simplification in BenillaQuestLogList_Update, -- where the ref keeps a separate right-justified $parentTag FontString), so the ref's -- gsub over our label would post "Quest 1 (Complete)". The API title is exactly the -- string the ref's own trim yields — same result, different expression. `ChatFrameEditBox -- and` guards a window test that hasn't loaded ChatFrame.xml (BenillaPaperDollSlot_OnClick's -- precedent). -- -- Guard order inside the watch arm matches the ref exactly: already watched → unwatch, -- unconditionally; else zero objectives (QUEST_WATCH_NO_OBJECTIVES) or the watch list -- full (QUEST_WATCH_TOO_MANY) put the ref's red line on the errors frame -- (UIErrorsFrame:AddMessage, the ref's own call — lua:490/495), else watch it. The ref calls QuestWatch_Update() itself -- right after each Add/RemoveQuestWatch (same two call sites) — it does NOT lean on -- the QUEST_LOG_UPDATE/QUEST_WATCH_UPDATE events alone for this, since neither engine -- fires an event off a plain Add/RemoveQuestWatch call; we mirror that exactly. if mouseButton == "LeftButton" and IsShiftKeyDown() then local title = GetQuestLogTitle(index) if ChatFrameEditBox and ChatFrameEditBox:IsVisible() then -- The visibility test stays HERE, not in the helper: it is the ref's own fork -- (l.474/478) — with chat open this click never watches, and the helper's -- return would conflate "chat closed" with "nothing to post". BenillaChatEdit_InsertLink(title) elseif IsQuestWatched(index) then -- Clearing the timer too: a lingering timed entry would later expire and -- silently unwatch a re-added MANUAL watch. if title then BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS[title] = nil end RemoveQuestWatch(index) QuestWatch_Update() elseif GetNumQuestLeaderBoards(index) == 0 then -- ref QUEST_WATCH_NO_OBJECTIVES, red, straight onto the errors frame. UIErrorsFrame:AddMessage("This quest has no objectives to track", 1.0, 0.1, 0.1) elseif GetNumQuestWatches() >= BENILLA_QUESTLOG_MAX_WATCHES then -- ref QUEST_WATCH_TOO_MANY, red. UIErrorsFrame:AddMessage("You may only watch " .. BENILLA_QUESTLOG_MAX_WATCHES .. " quests at a time", 1.0, 0.1, 0.1) else -- A manual watch is PERMANENT (ref: QUEST_WATCH_NO_EXPIRE) — drop any timed -- entry the auto-watch may have armed for it. if title then BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS[title] = nil end AddQuestWatch(index) QuestWatch_Update() end end -- pin §5: every click (shifted/right-clicked or not) ends in select + a full repaint. SelectQuestLogEntry(index) BenillaQuestLogFrame_Update() end
-- The fold-all tab (ref QuestLogCollapseAllButton_OnClick, QuestLogFrame.lua:554-563): -- index 0 = every header; the tab's own +/- icon tracks the all-state. function QuestLogCollapseAllButton_OnClick() local b = getglobal("QuestLogCollapseAllButton") if b.allCollapsed then b.allCollapsed = nil b:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-MinusButton-Up") ExpandQuestHeader(0) else b.allCollapsed = 1 b:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-PlusButton-Up") CollapseQuestHeader(0) end end
-- pin §2's QuestLog_SetFirstValidSelection/QuestLog_GetFirstSelectableQuest -- (QuestLogFrame.lua:293-296, :565-582): if nothing is selected, pick the first non-header row. function QuestLog_SetFirstValidSelection() if GetQuestLogSelection() ~= 0 then return end local numEntries = GetNumQuestLogEntries() for i = 1, numEntries do local _, _, _, isHeader = GetQuestLogTitle(i) if not isHeader then SelectQuestLogEntry(i) return end end end
function BenillaQuestLogList_Update() local numEntries, numQuests = GetNumQuestLogEntries() -- Ref QuestLogFrame.lua:123-124 with QUEST_LOG_COUNT_TEMPLATE inlined verbatim -- (GlobalStrings.lua:3236): gold "Quests:" label, white count via the |cff markup; the -- pill's middle piece then shrinks to the text (ref sizes it every update). The >10 -- guard skips the first-ever paint, where the host hasn't measured the string yet -- (GetWidth 0 would collapse the pill; the next update — and every one after — sizes it). getglobal("QuestLogCount"):SetText(string.format("Quests: |cffffffff%d/%d|r", numQuests, MAX_QUESTLOG_QUESTS)) local countWidth = getglobal("QuestLogCount"):GetWidth() if countWidth and countWidth > 10 then getglobal("QuestLogCountMiddle"):SetWidth(countWidth) end
-- v1 empty state (pin §2 drives a whole separate EmptyQuestLogFrame; simplified here to -- one message string + hidden rows, see this file's header comment). NOTE: throughout -- this file "hiding" text is a blank SetText(""), never a Show/Hide call — exactly how -- `QuestFrame.xml`'s BenillaQuest_HideAll blanks its texts instead of hiding them. That -- convention predates region Show/Hide (`region.rs` has the real pair now, and the -- loader honours hidden= on regions); an empty string draws nothing, so it is equivalent -- either way and the idiom stays for consistency with the sibling windows. local abandonButton = getglobal("QuestLogAbandonButton") if numEntries == 0 then getglobal("QuestLogEmptyText"):SetText("Your quest log is empty.") abandonButton:Disable() else getglobal("QuestLogEmptyText"):SetText("") abandonButton:Enable() end
-- Clamp the faux-scroll offset (pin §2's FauxScrollFrame_Update clamp). local maxOffset = numEntries - QUESTS_DISPLAYED if maxOffset < 0 then maxOffset = 0 end if questLogOffset > maxOffset then questLogOffset = maxOffset end if questLogOffset < 0 then questLogOffset = 0 end
local selection = GetQuestLogSelection()
for i = 1, QUESTS_DISPLAYED do local button = getglobal("QuestLogTitle" .. i) local index = i + questLogOffset if index <= numEntries then local title, level, tag, isHeader, isCollapsed, isComplete = GetQuestLogTitle(index) local text = title or "" if isHeader then -- Ref QuestLogFrame.lua:146-159: a header shows the plus/minus fold icon -- (its NormalTexture — the row template declares the 16x16 LEFT+3 slot), -- the plus-glow hover art, no indent, no tag, no watch check. if isCollapsed then button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-PlusButton-Up") else button:SetNormalTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-MinusButton-Up") end button.foldHighlight:SetTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-PlusButton-Hilight") else -- Ref l.161-166: quest rows clear both state slots and indent two spaces. text = " " .. text button:SetNormalTexture("") button.foldHighlight:SetTexture("") if isComplete == 1 then text = text .. " (Complete)" elseif isComplete == -1 then text = text .. " (Failed)" end end -- pin §2: the ref recolors via a SEPARATE right-side tag FontString; one combined -- string (title + tag suffix, above) is our v1 simplification — see this widget's -- own template comment. button.text:SetText(text) button.questIndex = index if isHeader then local c = QuestDifficultyColor["header"] button.text:SetTextColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) else local c = GetDifficultyColor(level) button.text:SetTextColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) end -- pin §2's $parentCheck: the per-row watch checkbox. SetTexture(path)/ -- SetTexture(nil) as the show/hide toggle — the icon-slot blanking pattern -- (`BenillaBagSlot_Update` etc.). (Regions DO have Show/Hide these days — -- region.rs; this site just predates it and the pattern is equivalent.) if not isHeader and IsQuestWatched(index) then button.check:SetTexture("Interface\\Buttons\\UI-CheckBox-Check") else button.check:SetTexture(nil) end button:Show() else button.questIndex = nil button:Hide() end end
-- The selection highlight follows the row only while it is inside the visible scroll -- window (pin §5, QuestLog_SetSelection QuestLogFrame.lua:330-340) — a selection scrolled -- off-screen still holds state, but the highlight itself doesn't show until the list -- scrolls back to it. Ref l.337-339 verbatim: the glow rides at (5,0) on the row and is -- vertex-colored to the row's own difficulty color (that green bar in the ref shot IS -- this vertex color on the white ADD gradient). local hl = getglobal("QuestLogSelectHighlight") if selection > questLogOffset and selection <= questLogOffset + QUESTS_DISPLAYED and selection <= numEntries then local selButton = getglobal("QuestLogTitle" .. (selection - questLogOffset)) local _, selLevel, _, selIsHeader = GetQuestLogTitle(selection) if selIsHeader then local c = QuestDifficultyColor["header"] getglobal("QuestLogSkillHighlight"):SetVertexColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) else local c = GetDifficultyColor(selLevel) getglobal("QuestLogSkillHighlight"):SetVertexColor(c.r, c.g, c.b) end hl:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", selButton, "TOPLEFT", 5, 0) hl:Show() else hl:Hide() end end
function BenillaQuestLogFrame_OnMouseWheel(delta) -- WoW wheel convention: +1 per notch up, -1 down (ChatFrame.xml's own handler quotes the -- same convention). Up = earlier entries (offset toward 0); down = later entries. if delta > 0 then questLogOffset = questLogOffset - 1 else questLogOffset = questLogOffset + 1 end BenillaQuestLogList_Update() end
-- ── The detail page ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The detail pane's real ScrollFrame (decision 0112's mechanism, landed this session — this -- window used to be a fixed layout that simply clipped past the window's bottom edge, this -- file's header comment). `QuestLogDetailScroll`'s ScrollChild is -- `QuestLogDetailChild`: every FontString/Button below that used to live flat on -- `QuestLogFrame` now lives on that child instead (the 0088 §2 flat-frame constraint -- this file's header comment quoted DIED with the 0112 resolver fixpoint — child frames -- render their own `<Layers>` regions again), so its subtree clips at the ScrollFrame's own -- rect and scrolls independent of the rest of the window. -- -- The child has no *reported* height from the engine (a Frame's height is its own SetSize — -- the resolver never grows a frame to fit content that overflows it, `script/mod.rs`'s -- region-resolution comment), so `BenillaQuestLogDetail_ResizeChild` below sums one by hand -- from the same fixed offsets/row heights this chain's own comments already cite, plus each -- auto-height FontString's OWN `GetHeight()` (region.rs: measured from the host font atlas -- once text is set — confirmed live, not a guess). That measurement is a FRAME LATE relative -- to *this* call (Lua runs before `resolve()`/the measure round-trip each tick, `ui_script/ -- mod.rs`'s drive loop) — a BRAND-NEW selection's text sizes off zero (never yet measured) -- on this very populate, understating the true height. Nothing guarantees a SECOND populate -- ever runs for the same stable selection (`QUEST_LOG_UPDATE` only fires on an actual data -- change — `ui_quest_log.rs`'s diffed feed — not every tick), so relying on "the next -- update self-heals it" silently under-sizes the child forever once the log goes quiet -- (caught on the ui-questlog capture: the reward text visibly clipped with the scrollbar -- never appearing). The honest fix is `BenillaQuestLogDetail_OnUpdate` below: it re-sums -- every frame the window is open (cheap — its own comment) until the measurement lands and -- the sum stops changing, which converges within a couple of frames of any repaint. A -- same-frame exact answer isn't available without an engine-side "resize to fit" primitive; -- this converges honestly instead of asserting a fiction.
-- A FontString's content height for the resize sum: blank text is a TRUE 0 regardless of -- what GetHeight() answers. Needed because `measured` (region.rs) is a one-way cache keyed -- off the LAST non-blank text — SetText("") never clears it (this engine has no live "0,0" -- the instant a string blanks, unlike the real client's font engine), so a freshly-blanked -- FontString would otherwise still report its previous text's height. A NON-blank string -- still reports last tick's measurement (this function's own header comment on the lag). function BenillaQuestLogDetail_TextHeight(fontString) local text = fontString:GetText() if not text or text == "" then return 0 end return fontString:GetHeight() end
-- Sums the child's needed height from this ONE chain's own fixed offsets (cited per term, -- each already documented at its own FontString/SetPoint above) + every auto-height -- FontString's measured `GetHeight()` + `rewardSectionHeight` (BenillaQuestLogRewards_Update's -- own return — its header-through-money layout has its own conditional branches, cheaper to -- total right where those branches already live than to re-derive them here). Then -- `UpdateScrollChildRect()` so the scrollbar (BenillaQuestLogDetailScroll_SyncBar) hears the -- new range. function BenillaQuestLogDetail_ResizeChild(objAnchorIndex, rewardSectionHeight) detailObjAnchorIndex = objAnchorIndex detailRewardHeight = rewardSectionHeight local title = getglobal("QuestLogQuestTitle") local objectivesText = getglobal("QuestLogObjectivesText") local description = getglobal("QuestLogDescription")
local objSpan if objAnchorIndex > 0 then objSpan = BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_OBJ_GAP + objAnchorIndex * BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_OBJ_ROW + (objAnchorIndex - 1) * BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_OBJ_STEP + BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_OBJ_GAP else objSpan = BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_OBJ_GAP end -- The countdown row, when the selection has one (decision 1150): one more -10 hop and -- one more fixed 12px row ahead of the objectives, whether or not any objective follows -- it — both branches above start at the same ObjectivesText→next -10, so the delta is -- the same either way. Read off the ref's own hasTimer flag rather than a second -- parameter, so the OnUpdate re-check below re-sums it without threading state. if BenillaQuestLogHasTimer then objSpan = objSpan + BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_OBJ_GAP + BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_OBJ_ROW end
local height = BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_TOP + BenillaQuestLogDetail_TextHeight(title) + 5 -- QuestTitle -> ObjectivesText + BenillaQuestLogDetail_TextHeight(objectivesText) + objSpan + 18 -- DescriptionTitle: fixed span regardless of text (its own comment) + 5 -- DescriptionTitle -> Description + BenillaQuestLogDetail_TextHeight(description) + 15 -- Description -> RewardTitleText + rewardSectionHeight + BENILLA_QUESTLOG_DETAIL_BOTTOM_PAD
if height ~= detailLastAppliedHeight then detailLastAppliedHeight = height getglobal("QuestLogDetailChild"):SetHeight(height) getglobal("QuestLogDetailScroll"):UpdateScrollChildRect() end end
-- The re-check `QuestLogDetailScroll`'s own `<OnUpdate>` calls every frame the log -- window is open (`UiScript::tick`'s OnUpdate gate gates it on effective-visibility, so this -- costs nothing while the window is closed): re-sums the SAME inputs the last full populate -- computed (`BenillaQuestLogDetail_ResizeChild`'s own header comment on why a single populate -- isn't enough — the auto-height FontStrings' `GetHeight()` only reflects a NEW text's real -- measurement one tick after this function first set it). `ResizeChild`'s own -- detailLastAppliedHeight guard makes every one of these calls a no-op once the resize has -- converged (no host measurement changed since the last check). function BenillaQuestLogDetail_OnUpdate() BenillaQuestLogDetail_ResizeChild(detailObjAnchorIndex, detailRewardHeight) end
-- ref QuestLog_OnUpdate (QuestLogFrame.lua:96-105), re-expressed here including its -- UPDATE_DELAY throttle: the countdown is repainted ten times a second, not every frame — -- SecondsToTime's output only changes once a second, so anything faster is a re-measure of -- an identical string. The flag/accumulator pair is the ref's own (its two fields on -- QuestLogFrame; ours are file globals because our detail state already lives that way). function QuestLog_OnUpdate(elapsed) if not BenillaQuestLogHasTimer then return end BenillaQuestLogTimePassed = (BenillaQuestLogTimePassed or 0) + (elapsed or 0) if BenillaQuestLogTimePassed > BENILLA_QUESTLOG_UPDATE_DELAY then local left = GetQuestLogTimeLeft() getglobal("QuestLogTimerText"):SetText( BENILLA_TIME_REMAINING .. " " .. SecondsToTime(left or 0)) BenillaQuestLogTimePassed = 0 end end
-- Steps the detail ScrollFrame by `delta` px — the wheel handler and both scrollbar arrow -- buttons share this one path; SetVerticalScroll's own clamp (benilla-ui's `scrollframe.rs`) -- does the range-bounding, this function just supplies the signed step. function BenillaQuestLogDetailScroll_Step(delta) local sf = getglobal("QuestLogDetailScroll") sf:SetVerticalScroll(sf:GetVerticalScroll() + delta) end
-- Repaints the minimal scrollbar (this window's own scrollbar comment: VISUAL only, no -- drag) from the CURRENT offset/range — wired to both OnVerticalScroll (the value changed) -- and OnScrollRangeChanged (the content resized), the ref UIPanelScrollFrameTemplate's own -- pair (UIPanelTemplates.xml). Hides the whole bar when nothing overflows (range 0); disables -- either arrow at its own end, mirroring the ref's identical two Enable/Disable calls off a -- real Slider's min/max (there's no Slider here — this window's own comment on why). function BenillaQuestLogDetailScroll_SyncBar() local sf = getglobal("QuestLogDetailScroll") local value = sf:GetVerticalScroll() local range = sf:GetVerticalScrollRange() local bar = getglobal("QuestLogDetailScrollBar") if range <= 0 then bar:Hide() return end bar:Show() if value > 0 then getglobal("QuestLogDetailScrollUp"):Enable() else getglobal("QuestLogDetailScrollUp"):Disable() end if value < range then getglobal("QuestLogDetailScrollDown"):Enable() else getglobal("QuestLogDetailScrollDown"):Disable() end local travel = BENILLA_QUESTLOG_SCROLL_TRACK_H - BENILLA_QUESTLOG_SCROLL_THUMB_H local frac = value / range getglobal("QuestLogDetailScrollThumb"):SetPoint( "TOPLEFT", getglobal("QuestLogDetailScrollTrack"), "TOPLEFT", 0, -(frac * travel)) end
function BenillaQuestLogDetail_Clear() getglobal("QuestLogQuestTitle"):SetText("") getglobal("QuestLogObjectivesText"):SetText("") -- The ref clears hasTimer on the empty-log path too (QuestLog_Update, :108) — without -- it the per-tick repaint keeps writing a countdown into a pane with no selection, and -- the child height keeps paying for a row that isn't there. BenillaQuestLogHasTimer = nil getglobal("QuestLogTimerText"):SetText("") getglobal("QuestLogDescriptionTitle"):SetText("") getglobal("QuestLogDescription"):SetText("") for i = 1, MAX_OBJECTIVES do getglobal("QuestLogObjective" .. i):SetText("") end getglobal("QuestLogRewardTitleText"):SetText("") getglobal("QuestLogItemChooseText"):SetText("") getglobal("QuestLogItemReceiveText"):SetText("") for i = 1, BENILLA_QUESTLOG_MAX_ITEMS do getglobal("QuestLogChoice" .. i):Hide() getglobal("QuestLogReward" .. i):Hide() end BenillaMoney_Clear("QuestLogMoney") -- Nothing selected: the header-only span (BenillaQuestLogRewards_Update's own -- haveAnyReward==false case, 18px) is the right resize input here too. BenillaQuestLogDetail_ResizeChild(0, 18) end
-- Fill + show one reward/choice row. `getter` is GetQuestLogChoiceInfo or -- GetQuestLogRewardInfo (pin §6): both answer the shared 5-tuple `name, texture, count, -- quality, usable` — the same shape QuestFrame.xml's GetQuestItemInfo(kind, index) answers -- for the questgiver panels, just under quest-log-specific getter names instead of one -- kind-dispatched function. `kind` ("choice"/"reward") rides alongside because the LINK -- getter IS kind-dispatched — GetQuestLogItemLink(this.type, this:GetID()), ref -- QuestLogFrame.lua:545/549 — and because it is the ref's own `questItem.type` -- (QuestFrame.lua:369/476, the shared layout routine both windows run). function BenillaQuestLogItem_Set(button, getter, index, kind) local name, texture, count, quality, usable, itemId = getter(index) button.index = index button.kind = kind button.itemId = itemId -- ref QuestFrame.lua:388/490 ("-- For the tooltip"), the same stamp the giver window's -- BenillaQuestItem_Set makes: only the reward-SPELL row ever reads "spell" (l.445), and -- v1 builds none (GetQuestLogRewardSpell is nil — this file's header). The click arms -- below guard on it exactly as the ref does, so the guard is live when that row lands. button.rewardType = "item" button.quality = quality button.icon:SetTexture(texture or BENILLA_FALLBACK_ICON) button.name:SetText(name or "...") if (count or 1) > 1 then button.count:SetText(count) else button.count:SetText("") end local r, g, b = 1, 1, 1 if quality and BenillaTooltip_QualityColor then r, g, b = BenillaTooltip_QualityColor(quality) end button.name:SetTextColor(r, g, b) if usable then button.nameFrame:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) button.icon:SetVertexColor(1, 1, 1) else button.nameFrame:SetVertexColor(0.9, 0, 0) button.icon:SetVertexColor(0.9, 0, 0) end button:Show() end
-- ref QuestLogRewardItem_OnClick (QuestLogFrame.lua:542-552), the OnClick -- QuestLogRewardItemTemplate carries (ref QuestLogFrame.xml:118-120): CTRL previews the -- reward in the dressing room (decision 1060), SHIFT posts its link into an open chat edit -- box (decision 1059). There is no third arm here — a quest-log reward row is never -- selectable, so a plain click is inert, which is why these rows carried no OnClick before -- this arc. -- -- Guard-for-guard with the ref: ctrl is gated on `this.rewardType ~= "spell"` (l.544), and -- so is shift — but on the ELSEIF line itself (l.547), where the giver window's twin puts it -- inside (QuestFrame.lua:121). Same outcome, and kept where the ref puts it. (i - 2)), "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -2) else choice:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", getglobal("QuestLogChoice" .. (i - 1)), "TOPRIGHT", 1, 0) end else choice:Hide() end end

(i - 2)), "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -2) else reward:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", getglobal("QuestLogReward" .. (i - 1)), "TOPRIGHT", 1, 0) end else reward:Hide() end end

-- The section's total height, mirroring the branches above term-for-term (a money-only -- coin row adds no height of its own — it rides receiveText's own row, LEFT of it, not -- a new one — this window's own coin-anchor comment just above). local height = 18 -- RewardTitleText: fixed span regardless of text (its own comment) if haveAnyReward then if numChoices > 0 then local numChoiceRows = math.ceil(lastChoice / 2) height = height + 5 -- header -> chooseText + BenillaQuestLogDetail_TextHeight(chooseText) + 5 -- chooseText -> choice row 1 + numChoiceRows * 41 + (numChoiceRows - 1) * 2 end if haveFixed then height = height + 5 -- (last choice row, or the header) -> receiveText + BenillaQuestLogDetail_TextHeight(receiveText) if numRewards > 0 then local numRewardRows = math.ceil(lastReward / 2) height = height + 5 -- receiveText -> reward row 1 + numRewardRows * 41 + (numRewardRows - 1) * 2 end end end return height end
-- pin §3/§5's doNotScroll asymmetry (QuestLogFrame.lua:348/455-457, QUESTLOG-PIN.md's own -- section on it): a MANUAL reselect (`BenillaQuestLogTitle_OnClick`, no arg here) always -- snaps the detail pane's scroll back to the top; the QUEST_LOG_UPDATE data-refresh path -- (`BenillaQuestLogFrame_OnEvent` below) passes `doNotScroll=true` so a quest updating while -- already being read doesn't yank the player's scroll position out from under them. function BenillaQuestLogDetail_Update(doNotScroll) local selection = GetQuestLogSelection() if selection == 0 or selection > GetNumQuestLogEntries() then BenillaQuestLogDetail_Clear() if not doNotScroll then getglobal("QuestLogDetailScroll"):SetVerticalScroll(0) end return end

" - (Failed)" end getglobal("QuestLogQuestTitle"):SetText(title or "")

No RequiredMoney branch here (this file's documented v1 gap: no -- widget backs GetQuestLogRequiredMoney yet) — that ref branch collapses into the rest. -- The objective-less TIMED branch (ref :432-437) is kept: a timed quest with no -- leaderboard lines hangs the header off the countdown row, not off ObjectivesText. local objAnchorIndex = math.min(numObjectives, MAX_OBJECTIVES) local descTitle = getglobal("QuestLogDescriptionTitle") if objAnchorIndex > 0 then descTitle:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", getglobal("QuestLogObjective" .. objAnchorIndex), "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -10) elseif questTimer then descTitle:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", getglobal("QuestLogTimerText"), "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -10) else descTitle:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", getglobal("QuestLogObjectivesText"), "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -10) end

-- ── The always-visible quest-watch tracker (QuestWatchFrame) ───────────────────────── -- Ref QuestWatch_Update (QuestLogFrame.lua:602-663), re-expressed onto the flat 30-line pool -- (the frame's own XML comment): every paint re-anchors each used line — a quest TITLE drops -- -5 below the previous line (ref -4 under its 13px boxes; ours are measured 12s, same -- pitch), an OBJECTIVE drops -1 (ref 0) — writes " - "-prefixed objective rows colored by -- the ref law (finished WHITE, unfinished 0.8-gray; the title dark-gold 0.75/0.61/0 until -- every objective completes, then full gold), sizes the frame to the content (width -- maxW+10 growing LEFT off the TOPRIGHT anchor, height lines×13), recolors the log -- window's Track dot, and hides the pool's trailing lines. `GetQuestIndexForWatch(w)` -- answers each watch's CURRENT log index (it follows the quest across a log shuffle — -- `quest_log.rs`'s id-keyed watch set), exactly like the ref. function QuestWatch_Update() local watchTextIndex = 1 local maxWidth = 0 for i = 1, GetNumQuestWatches() do local questIndex = GetQuestIndexForWatch(i) if questIndex then local numObjectives = GetNumQuestLeaderBoards(questIndex) if numObjectives > 0 then local titleLine = getglobal("QuestWatchLine" .. watchTextIndex) titleLine:SetText(GetQuestLogTitle(questIndex) or "") if watchTextIndex > 1 then titleLine:ClearAllPoints() titleLine:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", getglobal("QuestWatchLine" .. (watchTextIndex - 1)), "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -5) end titleLine:Show() if titleLine:GetStringWidth() > maxWidth then maxWidth = titleLine:GetStringWidth() end watchTextIndex = watchTextIndex + 1 local objectivesCompleted = 0 for j = 1, numObjectives do local text, kind, finished = GetQuestLogLeaderBoard(j, questIndex) if not text or text == "" then text = kind or "" end local line = getglobal("QuestWatchLine" .. watchTextIndex) line:SetText(" - " .. text) if finished then line:SetTextColor(1, 1, 1) objectivesCompleted = objectivesCompleted + 1 else line:SetTextColor(0.8, 0.8, 0.8) end line:ClearAllPoints() line:SetPoint("TOPLEFT", getglobal("QuestWatchLine" .. (watchTextIndex - 1)), "BOTTOMLEFT", 0, -1) line:Show() if line:GetStringWidth() > maxWidth then maxWidth = line:GetStringWidth() end watchTextIndex = watchTextIndex + 1 end if objectivesCompleted == numObjectives then titleLine:SetTextColor(1, 0.82, 0) else titleLine:SetTextColor(0.75, 0.61, 0) end end end end -- The log window's Track dot (the ref's tracking-indicator tail): green with ≥1 -- watch, red with none. if GetNumQuestWatches() > 0 then getglobal("QuestLogTrackTracking"):SetVertexColor(0, 1.0, 0) else getglobal("QuestLogTrackTracking"):SetVertexColor(1.0, 0, 0) end local frame = getglobal("QuestWatchFrame") if watchTextIndex == 1 then frame:Hide() return end frame:Show() frame:SetHeight(watchTextIndex * 13) if maxWidth > 0 then frame:SetWidth(maxWidth + 10) end -- The GetStringWidth reads above are extract-measured — a frame stale after a text -- change — so the OnUpdate sizing tail re-reads them for two frames and converges. frame.used_lines = watchTextIndex - 1 frame.resize_pending = 2 for i = watchTextIndex, BENILLA_QUESTWATCH_LINES do getglobal("QuestWatchLine" .. i):Hide() end end
-- ── Auto quest watching (ref QuestLogFrame.lua:702-786; AUTO_QUEST_WATCH defaults "1" — -- "Quests are automatically watched for 5 minutes when you achieve a quest objective."). -- BENILLA_QUEST_PROGRESS(questLogIndex) — our own engine event — arms a 300 s timed -- watch: a manual shift-click watch is permanent (no timer entry) and never downgraded, -- fresh progress re-arms a timed one, expiry unwatches, and a full watch list evicts the -- timed entry nearest expiry (never a manual one). Timers key by quest TITLE (stable -- across log shuffles; the engine's watch set is id-keyed — the ref's index-keyed -- QUEST_WATCH_LIST bookkeeping is transcribed to its observable law, not its -- iterate-while-mutating quirks). -- -- Why NOT the native QUEST_WATCH_UPDATE the ref Lua consumes: the §5-verified engine -- (wow-re quest-update-ui-feedback-law.md, handler 0x5e5ad0) fires that event with the -- quest's 1-based WATCH-LIST position — 0 when unwatched — while the ref's -- AutoQuestWatch_Update(arg1) treats arg1 as a quest-LOG index: the shipped 1.12 chain -- is broken at exactly that seam (an unwatched quest's progress arrives as 0, and -- AddQuestWatch(0) no-ops), so the advertised auto-watch never actually adds a quest. -- We keep the advertised behavior — the feature the option tooltip documents — off the -- benilla event that carries what the Lua needed; a deliberate intent-over-letter -- divergence (the fold-back decision record). -- -- The FLAG is the ref's own uvar, under the ref's own name since decision 1136 — it was -- BENILLA_AUTO_QUEST_WATCH (a boolean) while nothing could change it. It is a "1"/"0" -- string now because that is what an options row writes and what the reference's own -- consumers compare against; the Interface page's "Automatic Quest Tracking" row drives it. -- -- Which is the SECOND break in this feature, independent of the event seam above and just -- as fatal: 1.12 assigns `AUTO_QUEST_WATCH = 1` — the NUMBER — at UIOptionsFrame.lua:122, -- while every consumer tests `AUTO_QUEST_WATCH == "1"` (QuestLogFrame.lua:64/68) and the -- checkbox loads on the same string compare. In Lua 5.0 `1 ~= "1"`, so on a fresh install -- the option paints UNCHECKED and the auto-watch is dead, despite the table declaring -- `default = "1"`; it only comes alive once the player clicks the box, which writes the -- string. We ship the string, so the advertised default is the real one. AUTO_QUEST_WATCH = "1" RegisterForSave("AUTO_QUEST_WATCH") BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMER = 300 BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS = {}
function BenillaQuestWatch_RemoveByTitle(title) for w = 1, GetNumQuestWatches() do local questIndex = GetQuestIndexForWatch(w) if questIndex and GetQuestLogTitle(questIndex) == title then RemoveQuestWatch(questIndex) return end end end
function AutoQuestWatch_Update(questIndex) if AUTO_QUEST_WATCH ~= "1" or not questIndex then return end local title = GetQuestLogTitle(questIndex) if not title then return end if IsQuestWatched(questIndex) then if BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS[title] then BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS[title] = BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMER end return end if GetNumQuestLeaderBoards(questIndex) == 0 then return end if GetNumQuestWatches() >= BENILLA_QUESTLOG_MAX_WATCHES then local lowestTitle, lowestTimer = nil, BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMER + 1 for t, timer in pairs(BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS) do if timer < lowestTimer then lowestTitle, lowestTimer = t, timer end end if not lowestTitle then return end -- every slot is a manual watch: no eviction BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS[lowestTitle] = nil BenillaQuestWatch_RemoveByTitle(lowestTitle) end AddQuestWatch(questIndex) BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS[title] = BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMER end
function AutoQuestWatch_OnUpdate(elapsed) local expired = nil for title, timer in pairs(BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS) do if timer - elapsed <= 0 then expired = expired or {} table.insert(expired, title) else BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS[title] = timer - elapsed end end if expired then for _, title in ipairs(expired) do BENILLA_QUEST_WATCH_TIMERS[title] = nil BenillaQuestWatch_RemoveByTitle(title) end QuestWatch_Update() BenillaQuestLogList_Update() -- the log's row ticks follow (ref: QuestLog_Update) end end
function BenillaQuestWatchFrame_OnLoad(frame) -- Repaints on all three: QUEST_LOG_UPDATE (every log change — the ref's own -- QuestLog_OnEvent repaints QuestWatch_Update() off it too, QuestLogFrame.lua:57-70), -- the native QUEST_WATCH_UPDATE (arg1 = the WATCH-LIST index, 0 if unwatched — kept -- for repaint + any future addon, never for auto-watch: the divergence comment -- above), and BENILLA_QUEST_PROGRESS (arg1 = the quest-LOG index) which feeds the -- auto-watch. frame:RegisterEvent("QUEST_LOG_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("QUEST_WATCH_UPDATE") frame:RegisterEvent("BENILLA_QUEST_PROGRESS") QuestWatch_Update() end
function BenillaQuestWatchFrame_OnEvent(frame) if event == "BENILLA_QUEST_PROGRESS" then AutoQuestWatch_Update(arg1) QuestWatch_Update() elseif event == "QUEST_WATCH_UPDATE" or event == "QUEST_LOG_UPDATE" then QuestWatch_Update() end end
-- The watch frame's OnUpdate carries the ref's auto-watch timer decay (ref -- QuestLogFrame.xml:1140-1144 — the ALWAYS-VISIBLE frame hosts it, so timers tick with -- the log closed; hidden-with-no-watches is safe, an empty watch set has no timers) plus -- our sizing-convergence tail (QuestWatch_Update's own comment). function BenillaQuestWatchFrame_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) AutoQuestWatch_OnUpdate(elapsed or 0) if frame.resize_pending and frame.resize_pending > 0 then frame.resize_pending = frame.resize_pending - 1 local maxw = 0 for i = 1, (frame.used_lines or 0) do local w = getglobal("QuestWatchLine" .. i):GetStringWidth() if w > maxw then maxw = w end end if maxw > 0 then frame:SetWidth(maxw + 10) end end end
-- ── Window lifecycle ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- `doNotScroll` (pin §5's asymmetry, threaded through to `BenillaQuestLogDetail_Update`): -- absent/falsy for a manual call (a row click, the window's own OnShow); `true` from the -- QUEST_LOG_UPDATE event handler below. function BenillaQuestLogFrame_Update(doNotScroll) QuestLog_SetFirstValidSelection() BenillaQuestLogList_Update() -- pin §5, QuestLog_OnEvent (QuestLogFrame.lua:57-63): the detail pane only repaints while -- the window is visible — the list rebuild above runs unconditionally either way. if getglobal("QuestLogFrame"):IsVisible() then BenillaQuestLogDetail_Update(doNotScroll) end end
function BenillaQuestLogFrame_OnLoad(frame) frame:RegisterEvent("QUEST_LOG_UPDATE") end
function BenillaQuestLogFrame_OnEvent(frame) if event == "QUEST_LOG_UPDATE" then -- pin §5: the event-driven refresh path passes doNotScroll=true (QuestLogFrame.lua:62 -- passes `1`) — a quest updating while already being read must not yank the reader's -- scroll position back to the top.
